Adathoda.short_botanical_description: An evergreen shrub featuring lanceolate leaves and white, tubular two-lipped flowers marked with purple streaks.
Adathoda.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic and traditional herbal practices as an oral decoction for soothing respiratory discomforts and throat irritations.

Allium_Cepa.short_botanical_description: Spherical umbel inflorescences composed of numerous small, white to pale purple star-shaped flowers atop hollow green scapes.
Allium_Cepa.traditional_uses: Commonly reported in folk remedies and traditional culinary wellness routines for supporting digestive comfort and general immunity.

Banana.short_botanical_description: Large teardrop-shaped dark purple to reddish bracts enclosing tubular yellowish flowers arranged in whorled rows.
Banana.traditional_uses: Traditionally consumed in South Asian and Southeast Asian culinary traditions and folk routines for supporting digestive health.

Black_cumin.short_botanical_description: Delicate pale blue to white solitary flowers with 5 to 10 petals surrounding intricate green seed capsules.
Black_cumin.traditional_uses: Seeds and floral extracts are traditionally used in Unani and Ayurvedic traditions for general digestive support and respiratory wellbeing.

Bush Clock Vine.short_botanical_description: Erect woody shrub featuring trumpet-shaped deep royal blue or purple flowers with bright yellow throats.
Bush Clock Vine.traditional_uses: Commonly cultivated as an ornamental flower; reported in regional traditional practices for mild topical cooling applications.

Champaka.short_botanical_description: Highly fragrant narrow yellowish-orange to cream petals arranged in a cup-like spiral, growing on large evergreen trees.
Champaka.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic aromatherapy, floral oils, and spiritual ceremonies for promoting relaxation and mental calmness.

Chitrak.short_botanical_description: Perennial subshrub with terminal racemes of white salverform flowers covered in sticky glandular hairs.
Chitrak.traditional_uses: Roots and floral extracts are traditionally utilized in Ayurvedic preparations for digestive stimulation and skin wellness applications.

Common Lanthana.short_botanical_description: Dense umbrella-like flat-topped clusters of small tubular flowers displaying color variations from yellow, orange, to pink and red.
Common Lanthana.traditional_uses: Commonly reported in folk traditions for mild topical poultices; noted in traditional literature for aromatic leaf oils.

Crown Flower.short_botanical_description: Waxy, crown-shaped flowers in shades of white or lavender with a prominent central stamen column, surrounded by thick obovate leaves.
Crown Flower.traditional_uses: Used in traditional Indian ceremonies and Ayurvedic folk applications for external joint warmth; handles require caution due to milky latex.

Datura.short_botanical_description: Large, fragrant trumpet-shaped flowers in white, purple, or yellow, producing spiny globose seed capsules.
Datura.traditional_uses: Historically cited in traditional literature for specific external poultice applications; requires strict expert supervision due to natural alkaloids.

Four O' Clock Flower.short_botanical_description: Fragrant trumpet-shaped flowers opening in late afternoon, available in vibrant magenta, yellow, white, or variegated hues.
Four O' Clock Flower.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in indigenous herbal practices for mild topical soothing and as a natural flower dye source.

Hibiscus.short_botanical_description: Large, showy bell-shaped flowers with five broad petals and a long, prominent central staminal column.
Hibiscus.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in floral teas and herbal hair oil preparations for supporting hair vitality and skin hydration.

Honey Suckle.short_botanical_description: Fragrant tubular two-lipped flowers that open white and mature to golden yellow, growing on trailing vines.
Honey Suckle.traditional_uses: Commonly reported in traditional East Asian herbal teas and remedies for cooling body comfort during seasonal changes.

Indian Mallow.short_botanical_description: Golden-yellow solitary flowers with five overlapping petals and heart-shaped serrated leaves.
Indian Mallow.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic formulations for supporting muscular comfort, oral hygiene rinses, and general stamina.

Jatropha.short_botanical_description: Star-shaped bright red or pink 5-petaled flowers arranged in terminal cymes against glossy dark green leaves.
Jatropha.traditional_uses: Widely grown as an ornamental garden plant; regional folk accounts describe traditional usage of leaf extracts for topical washes.

Malabar Melastome.short_botanical_description: Vibrant mauve-to-purple 5-petaled flowers with distinctive yellow stamens and ribbed oval leaves.
Malabar Melastome.traditional_uses: Leaves and flowers are traditionally used in Southeast Asian folk wellness routines for gentle astringent mouth rinses and skin comfort.

Marigold.short_botanical_description: Dense pom-pom-like flower heads with bright yellow, orange, or golden ray florets and aromatic pinnate leaves.
Marigold.traditional_uses: Widely used in traditional cultural garlands and herbal ointments for supporting skin comfort and eye wellness routines.

Nagapoovu.short_botanical_description: Large, fragrant reddish-pink flowers with a hood-like structure covering the central stamens, blooming directly on tree trunks.
Nagapoovu.traditional_uses: Revered in traditional spiritual practices; regional ethnomedical reports note flower extracts used in traditional soothing baths.

Nityakalyani.short_botanical_description: Salverform 5-petaled flowers in shades of pink, rose, or white with a darker red central eye.
Nityakalyani.traditional_uses: Traditionally cited in folk remedies for supporting general metabolic wellness; source of well-studied plant alkaloids.

Pinwheel.short_botanical_description: Pure white, 5-lobed pinwheel-shaped petals with a central yellow throat blooming against shiny dark green foliage.
Pinwheel.traditional_uses: Flowers are traditionally used in temple rituals and floral water drops reported in Ayurvedic traditions for soothing eye hygiene.

Rose.short_botanical_description: Fragrant multi-petaled flowers in varied hues of red, pink, and white supported by thorny stems.
Rose.traditional_uses: Rose petals and rose water are traditionally used in Unani and Ayurvedic traditions for skin hydration, emotional relaxation, and culinary aromatics.

Shankupushpam.short_botanical_description: Striking deep cobalt blue, conch-shell-shaped solitary flowers with a white or pale yellow center growing on climbing vines.
Shankupushpam.traditional_uses: Traditionally valued in Ayurvedic Medhya Rasayana formulations for supporting cognitive focus, memory clarity, and herbal teas.

Spider Lily.short_botanical_description: Pure white spider-like blossoms featuring long slender petals extending from a central delicate stamina cup.
Spider Lily.traditional_uses: Popular ornamental blossom; regional folk literature notes traditional warm bulb/leaf compresses for joint support.

Sunflower.short_botanical_description: Large composite flower head consisting of yellow ray florets surrounding a dense dark central disk of disk florets.
Sunflower.traditional_uses: Petals and seeds are traditionally used in wellness infusions and culinary oils rich in natural fatty acids and Vitamin E.

Sweet_pea.short_botanical_description: Fragrant butterfly-like flowers in pastel purples, pinks, and whites growing on tendril-bearing climbing stems.
Sweet_pea.traditional_uses: Cultivated primarily as an aromatic ornamental flower; valued in traditional garden displays and floral perfumery.

Thechi.short_botanical_description: Dense round clusters of small, tubular, 4-petaled bright scarlet or orange flowers growing on compact evergreen bushes.
Thechi.traditional_uses: Flowers and roots are traditionally used in Ayurvedic preparations for skin soothing, oral hygiene, and digestive wellbeing.

Thumba.short_botanical_description: Small, hooded white flowers arranged in dense whorled clusters along square pubescent stems.
Thumba.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in South Indian Ayurvedic traditions and Onam floral decorations, as well as nasal drops in traditional remedies for head comfort.

Touch Me Not.short_botanical_description: Fluffy, globe-like pinkish-purple ball flowers accompanied by compound leaves that fold inward immediately when touched.
Touch Me Not.traditional_uses: Traditionally utilized in Ayurvedic medicine for supporting urinary tract comfort, skin cooling, and healthy digestive function.

Tridax procumbens.short_botanical_description: Small daisy-like flower heads with white to pale yellow 3-toothed ray florets atop hairy, spreading stems.
Tridax procumbens.traditional_uses: Leaf juice and flower extract are widely reported in traditional folk remedies for supporting natural wound healing and soothing skin grazes.

Wild potato vine.short_botanical_description: Large funnel-shaped white morning-glory-like flowers with deep pink to purple throats growing on trailing vines.
Wild potato vine.traditional_uses: Tuberous roots and flowers are documented in Native American traditional herbal practices; flagged for botanical confirmation due to regional variations.

Yellow Daisy.short_botanical_description: Bright yellow daisy-like solitary flower heads blooming on low-growing, creeping herbaceous stems.
Yellow Daisy.traditional_uses: Traditionally used in Ayurvedic herbs (Bhringraj substitute) for supporting hair health, liver wellness, and soothing bath preparations.
